1

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.60,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 31072021 at about 7.45 p.m., the Petitioner was proceeding in his motor cycle bearing No.KA02HH3218 near Tippagondanahalli village, Magadi main road, Tavarekere Hobli, Bangalore city.
At that time, a i20 car bearing No.KA02 MQ 4217 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against motor cycle.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down along with motor cycle and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Sri Lakshmi Multi Speciality hospital for first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedic hospital wherein he was treated as an inpatient.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedic hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as Supervisor and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/ p.m.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the i20 car and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the court through it's counsel and filed objections to the main petition.

In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.2, it denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of i20 car.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further it denied the issuance of policy in respect of i20 car.
It is further contended that the accident was not caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by its driver.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to negligence of petitioner himself.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 31072021 at about 7.45 p.m. near Tippagondanahalli village, Magadi Main road,
Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Paramesh M.H vs Rashe Pharma on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180472808/
2 i20 car bearing No.KA02MQ4217?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so.
How much and from whom?

3. What Order or Award?
5.
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.14.
He also got examined two witnesses as P.W.2 and PW.3 and got marked documents as per Ex.P15 to 18 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondents have not chosen to adduce any evidence.

6. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2, upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 7. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 31072021 at about 7.45 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the i20 car bearing No.KA02MQ4217 by its driver.
8.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the offending i20 car bearing No.KA02MQ4217 by its driver.
9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P14.
P.W.1 has reiterated the Petition averments in his chief affidavit.

Ex. P1 to Ex.P6 are the True copies of FIR, complaint, spot panchanama, police notice,
Wound certificate and charge sheet.
Ex . P.7
is the discharge summary, Ex.P.8 is the medical prescriptions.
Ex.P.9 is the medical bills.

Ex.P.10 is the wage slips from January 2021 to June 2021,
Ex.P.11 is the estimation, Ex.P.12 is the notarised copy of aadhar card and Ex.P.13 is the notarised card of employment identity card of PW.1
. Ex.P.14 is the advance receipt.

Ex.P.15 is the OPD record,
Ex.P.16 is the Xray, Ex.P.17 is the authorisation letter and Ex.P.18 is the entire inpatient records.

10. Upon going through Ex.P1 and 2 i.e., FIR and Complaint, same is evident that on the complaint lodged before Tavarekere Police station, the SHO of the concerned Police Station has registered a case against the driver of i20 car bearing No.KA02MQ4217 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
The documents Ex. P.1 to 4, 6 and IMV report justify the fact of involvement of KA02JY2015 and the offending vehicle in the accident that occurred on 31.07.2021.
the document Ex.P.3 discloses the fact that in the presence of pancha witnesses, the IO concerned has drawn the spot mahazar.

The document Ex.P.5 discloses the fact as a result of accident, the petitioner sustained such injuries mentioned in the said document which are grievous in nature as Paramesh M.H vs Rashe Pharma on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180472808/
3 opined by the doctor concerned.

entities.text: Paramesh M.H vs Rashe Pharma on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The document Ex.P.6 i.e., the charge sheet clearly establishes the fact that after thorough investigation IO has charge sheeted the driver of i20 car bearing No.KA 02MQ4217 for the offences punishable under Secs.279, 338 of IPC.
11. Further, P.W.1 examined Dr.S.A.Somashekar as P.W.2 and got marked OPD card and Xray at Ex.P.15 and16.
He also reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.

12. Further, P.W.1 examined medical record officer of Sanjay Gandhi hospital as P.W.3 and got marked authorisation letter and entire inpatient records at Ex.P.17 and 18.
13.
To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross examination P.W.1 has denied the other suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioner.
14. Further, the Respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence to rebut the evidence of petitioner.
In addition to this, the IO after thorough investigation filed a charge sheet against the driver of i20 car bearing No.KA02MQ4217.
The said charge sheet admittedly remained unchallenged till date.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the i20 car bearing No.KA02MQ4217 by its driver and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.

15. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of i20 car bearing No.KA02MQ4217, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
16. According to the Petitioner, he sustained grievous injuries.
As per the Wound Certificate, the Petitioner has sustained following injuries.
1. Crush injury of the right leg of ankle exposing deeper structure.
2. Swelling, tenderness, deformity of right thigh.
Xray reveal right femur shaft and right leg crush injury with implant in situ.
The doctor has opined that injuries are grievous in nature.
Further, P.W.2 Dr.S.A.Somashekar has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
17. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 39 years.
He has produced aadhar card at Ex.P.12 to prove his age.
As per aadhar card, date of birth is shown as 18.06.1983.
The accident has taken place on 31.07.2021.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was taken as 38 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.

Paramesh M.H vs Rashe Pharma on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180472808/
4 18.
Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as supervisor and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/p.m.
In this regard, he has produced wage slips for the months of January 2021 to June 2021 to prove his avocation.
The documents produced at Ex.P.10 discloses the fact that one Mr.Paramesh N.H. was drawing a salary of sum of Rs.18,000/.p.m.
The petitioner admittedly not examined the author of the said document.
Even during his cross examination, PW.1 admits to have not produced any supportive documents to show that he was drawing a sum of Rs.30,000.
p.m. as asserted
. Moreover, PW.1 has deposed that salary was handed over by the employer to the hands of employee.
In the absence of supportive evidence of author of Ex. P.10, it is not safe to blindly rely upon Ex. P.10 to assess the monthly income of the petitioner.

However, keeping in mind the guideliness issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, considering the date of occurrence of accident, if the income of the petitioner per month is taken at Rs.15,000/ for the purpose of assessment, it would meet the ends of justice and equity.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.15,000/ is considered as monthly income of the petitioner.
19. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
20.
The petitioner has deposed that due to the injuries he cannot do his regular activities, cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier and he has become too weak.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
21.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
22.
The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 0208 2021 to 30082021 at Sanjay Gandhi hospital.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient is 29 days.
23. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/ under this head (@ Rs.15,000/ per month).
IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
Paramesh M.H vs Rashe Pharma on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180472808/
5 24.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
25. The Petitioner has deposed that he spent Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical expenses.
The petitioner has produced 58 medical bills at Ex.P.9 amounting to Rs.68,386/.
I have perused the same carefully.
Careful perusal of Ex.P.9 justifies the fact that petitioner has furnished medical bills to a sum of Rs.88,386/.

The document Ex.P.14 is the advance receipts for a sum of Rs.46,450/.
During cross examinationn of PW.1 there is no serious dispute made regarding the medical bills.
However, the payments made vide advance receipts shall be deducted from the total claim of medical expenses.

As such from Rs.88,386/ a sum of Rs.46,450 is deducted and the petitioner is entitled for claim of medical expenses to the tune of Rs.41,936/ which is rounded off to Rs.42,000/ as a compensation under this head.

VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
26.

The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and due to the injuries he cannot do his regular activities, cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier and he has become too weak
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

27. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.S.A.Somashekar as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
Further, he got marked OPD card and Xray at Ex.P.15 and 16.
He assessed total disability of his whole body at 48%.
28. In the crossexamination PW.2 has stated that he has not personally treated the petitioner earlier,
He has admitted the suggestion that he has assessed the disability of the petitioner of right lower limb.
He has admitted that he has not issued any estimation regarding the expenses of Rs.40,000/ for removal of implants and he has not issued disability certificate.
It is also to be noted that there is admission from PW.2 of the fact that Ex. P.7 reflects regarding the surgery underwent by the petitioner for his right tibia 15 years ago.
There is also evidence on record that PW.2 not advised the petitioner to undergo any further surgery.
He has denied the suggestion that he has given higher rate of disability to the Petitioner.

29. Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on hand and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, upon consideration of the fact that the petitioner got examined himself before this court as PW.1 and also tendered for cross examination done at length by the learned advocate for respondent No.2 during which he could be Paramesh M.H vs Rashe Pharma on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180472808/
6 able to give rational answers to the questions and regarding the facts of the case and considering all these aspects, this Tribunal is of the opinion that it would be just and reasonable if the disability of the Petitioner is considered at 12%.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the age of Petitioner is 15.

With multiplier of 15, income of Rs.15,000/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 12%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.3,24,000/ (Rs.15,000/ x 12 = 1,80,000/, Rs.1.80,000/x 15 x 12/100 = 3,24,000/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,24,000/ under this head.
30. COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
Petitioner has produced Ex. P.11 document stating that he needs future medical expenses.
As observed above, the doctor/PW.2 admitted during his cross examination that he has not advised for any further surgery.
However, considering the fact that the petitioner may incur expenses in future in respect of the removal of implants, it appears just and reasonable to award sum of Rs.40,000/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
31.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 50,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 42,000/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 30,000/ laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.3,24,000/
7.
Future medical expenses Rs. 40,000/ Total Rs.5,34,000/
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.5,34,000/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
32. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of i20 car bearing No.KA02MQ4217.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of i20 car.
The Policy is valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.

Therefore,
Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Paramesh M.H vs Rashe Pharma on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180472808/
7
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
33. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.5,34,000/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.2, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E payment after proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.

33. ISSUE No. 3 :
In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.5,34,000/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.2, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E payment after proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
